Q: Changing an existing XF Android application to use Google App Signing. Which option should I select on the Play Store? A:

It depends, whats the extension for the keystore file that you have- .keystore or .jks? Since you mentioned that it's an existing app, so you would follow the instructions for Existing Apps, under "Opt in to app signing by Google Play" here.

If you are using a JKS file, simply select the "Java Keystore" option, or else if you have a KEYSTORE file, then select "Not using a Java Keystore". And then continue following the other steps.

Q: SQL SUM function not summing A:

The result rows with all zeros should stem from non-exercise rows. Rows with a sum, but a zero count, however, should not be possible with the code you are showing. That you don't get one result row per person, is because in your GROUP BY clause you ask explicitly for one result row per person and event.

Solution: Just filter the joined rows right away and group by person. You'll want to outer join this to the persons table, if you want to include persons without any matching data, or inner join it otherwise.

SELECT 
  p.person_name,
  COALESCE(x.gr_pct, 0) AS growth_percent,
  COALESCE(x.gr_cnt, 0) AS growth_count,
  COALESCE(x.co_pct, 0) AS composite_percent,
  COALESCE(x.co_cnt, 0) AS composite_count
FROM datawarehouse.dtbl_persons p
LEFT JOIN
(
  SELECT
    en.person_key,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Growth' THEN en.event_percentile END) AS gr_pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Growth' THEN 1 END) AS gr_cnt,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Composite' THEN en.event_percentile END) AS co_pct,
    SUM(CASE WHEN e.event_level = 'Composite' THEN 1 END) AS co_cnt
  FROM datawarehouse.ftbl_event_norms en
  JOIN datawarehouse.dtbl_events e ON e.events_key = en.events_key
  WHERE e.event_company = 'exercise'
    AND e.event_topic = 'quantitative'
    AND e.event_level IN ('Composite', 'Growth')
  GROUP BY en.person_key
 ) x ON x.person_key = p.person_key
ORDER BY p.person_name;

Q: need to display fields that has same name but different value when join in codeigniter A:

In addition to Mayank Pandeyz's answer:

Since you want to display both values in the field 'username', along with the alias, you can use CONCAT.

After you've set the aliases t1.username as uname1, t2.username as uname2 as Mayank Pandeyz described, you can "make" the field username like so: 

concat( t1.username, " ",t2.username ) AS username

This will create new column in the result, called as you want (in this case "username"). It will contain both values, separated by whitespace (separator is chosen by us).

                   events.col2 AS ev_col2,
